{{Short description|Sum of the reciprocal of the Mersenne numbers}}
The '''Erdős–Borwein constant''', named after [[Paul Erdős]] and [[Peter Borwein]], is the sum of the [[Reciprocal (mathematics)|reciprocals]] of the [[Mersenne prime|Mersenne number]]s.

By definition it is:

:<math>E=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{1}{2^n-1}\approx1.606695152415291763\dots</math><ref>{{OEIS|A065442}}</ref>

==Equivalent forms==
It can be proven that the following forms all sum to the same constant:

:<math>
E=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{1}{2^{n^2}}\frac{2^n+1}{2^n-1}
</math>

:<math>
E=\sum_{m=1}^{\infty}\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{1}{2^{mn}}
</math>

:<math>
E=1+\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{1}{2^n(2^n-1)}
</math>

:<math>
E=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{\sigma_0(n)}{2^n}
</math>

where σ<sub>0</sub>(''n'') = ''d''(''n'') is the [[divisor function]], a [[multiplicative function]] that equals the number of positive [[divisor]]s of the number ''n''. To prove the equivalence of these sums, note that they all take the form of [[Lambert series]] and can thus be resummed as such.<ref>The first of these forms is given by {{harvtxt|Knuth|1998}}, ex. 27, p. 157; Knuth attributes the transformation to this form to an 1828 work of [[Thomas Clausen (mathematician)|Clausen]].</ref>

==Irrationality==
In 1948, Erdős showed that the [[mathematical constant|constant]] ''E'' is an [[irrational number]].<ref>{{citation
 | last = Erdős | first = P. | author-link = Paul Erdős
 | journal = J. Indian Math. Soc. |series=New Series
 | mr = 0029405
 | pages = 63–66
 | title = On arithmetical properties of Lambert series
 | url = http://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1948-04.pdf
 | volume = 12
 | year = 1948}}.</ref> Later, Borwein provided an alternative proof.<ref>{{citation
 | last = Borwein | first = Peter B. | authorlink = Peter Borwein
 | doi = 10.1017/S030500410007081X
 | issue = 1
 | journal = [[Mathematical Proceedings of the Cambridge Philosophical Society]]
 | mr = 1162938
 | pages = 141–146
 | title = On the irrationality of certain series
 | volume = 112
 | year = 1992| bibcode = 1992MPCPS.112..141B | s2cid = 123705311 }}.</ref>

Despite its irrationality, the [[Binary numeral system|binary representation]] of the Erdős–Borwein constant may be calculated efficiently.<ref>{{harvtxt|Knuth|1998}} observes that calculations of the constant may be performed using Clausen's series, which converges very rapidly, and credits this idea to [[John Wrench]].</ref><ref>{{citation
 | last = Crandall | first = Richard | author-link = Richard Crandall
 | doi = 10.1515/integers-2012-0007
 | journal = Integers
 | page = A23
 | title = The googol-th bit of the Erdős–Borwein constant
 | volume = 12
 | year = 2012| issue = 5 | s2cid = 122157888 }}.</ref>

==Applications==
The Erdős–Borwein constant comes up in the [[average case analysis]] of the [[heapsort]] algorithm, where it controls the constant factor in the running time for converting an unsorted array of items into a heap.<ref>{{citation
 | last = Knuth | first = D. E. | author-link = Donald Knuth
 | edition = 2nd
 | location = Reading, MA
 | pages = 153–155
 | publisher = Addison-Wesley
 | title = [[The Art of Computer Programming]], Vol. 3: Sorting and Searching
 | year = 1998}}.</ref>
